chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, raising it (to the Imam), said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), when he ascended As-Safa, would face the Kaaba, then raise his hands and say:

"O Allah, forgive me every sin I have ever committed. If I return [to it], return forgiveness upon me, for You are the All-Forgiving, the Merciful. O Allah, do with me what You are worthy of, for if You do with me what You are worthy of, You will have mercy on me; and if You punish me, then You are Rich (self-sufficient) from my punishment, while I am in need of Your mercy. O He in whose mercy I am in need, have mercy on me. O Allah, do not do with me what I am worthy of, for if You do with me what I am worthy of, You will punish me, and You will not wrong me. I have become mindful of Your justice and do not fear Your injustice. O He who is Just and does not act unjustly, have mercy on me."
And it is recommended to stand on As-Safa, to prolong one's stay there, and to increase in supplication to his Lord. Narrated.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the hills between which pilgrims walk)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of Imam Ali (AS) when ascending As-Safa during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details Imam Ali’s (AS) specific supplication at As-Safa, emphasizing the theological balance between *khawf* (fear of one's unworthiness) and *raja'* (hope in Divine mercy). The text underscores the concept of *Adl* (Justice) as a source of comfort rather than dread, reflecting the Shia emphasis on God's attribute of being 'Just' yet 'Merciful'. It concludes with the juristic ruling (*hukm*) recommending prolonged standing and abundant supplication at this station, linking ritual action with spiritual introspection.
